source.title: Discovering and Causally Validating Emotion-Sensitive Neurons in Large Audio-Language Models
source.authors: Xiu-Tian Zhao; Björn W. Schuller; Berrak Sisman

page_placements.theme: Selective concept neurons exist and act causally

record.tranche_reason: The study measures emotion-sensitive neuron sets and their causal effects in audio-language models, but it does not test whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs or whether such polysemanticity is common.
record.gate_note: The paper's own neuron-intervention results are relevant to neuron specialization but do not measure the mixed-input behavior or other specific claims in V1–V7. The rows below record the closest related findings as versions none. Results cited from prior work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study identifies emotion-sensitive neuron sets in audio-language models and validates them causally with deactivation and steering. It never measures whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs. It does not report a share of polysemantic neurons. It does not test superposition, training causes, architecture effects, reinterpretation of canonical neurons, or measurement dependence. Neuron-specialization work is cited only as background, and the word polysemanticity does not appear. 'discusses' overstates the engagement; 'cites_only' fits better.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. It could add that the authors also report MAD/ConAct outperforming LAP/LAPE/random selection, ESNs clustering in layers 0, 6–8 and 19–22, partial and asymmetric cross-dataset transfer, and weak, inconsistent agnostic injection.
record.recipe_differences: The study identifies decoder MLP gate dimensions using emotion-conditioned activation statistics and applies inference-time deactivation or amplification; it does not reproduce the original sources' methods for investigating polysemanticity.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported causal effects depend on the neuron selector: MAD and ConAct produce stronger self-versus-cross effects than LAP and LAPE. Effects also vary with intervention budget, steering strength, and dataset, as described in the text.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating a 0.5% neuron set chosen by MAD or ConAct lowers target-emotion accuracy by about 11–15 points. Other emotions change by under 2 points. Amplifying the same set raises target accuracy by about 2–3 points, across three audio-language models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compact sets of decoder MLP gate units in audio-language models are causally and selectively involved in recognizing specific speech emotions.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger masks (r up to 1%) and stronger steering gains increase off-diagonal spillover. The authors read this as shared circuitry and coupling between emotion pathways.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Emotion-sensitive units partly share downstream computation across emotions.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The results concern emotion-conditioned neuron sets and SER performance, not individual neurons' responses to unrelated inputs. The paper reports macro-averaged effects across datasets in Table 1 without uncertainty estimates there; it notes that transfer is uneven and that agnostic injection is inconsistent.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 also reports RND, LAP, and LAPE results; these are selector comparisons for the adjacent emotion-recognition construct and do not directly measure any claim version. Dataset-specific deactivation and steering tables are in Appendix C.1 and C.2.

untested.parts: Decoder MLP gates of audio-language models are logged only on emotion-labelled speech. There is no measure of neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts, and no share of polysemantic neurons.
Superposition and feature capacity are not studied.
Initialization, regularization and training-noise causes are not studied.
There is no variation of activation function, architecture or training. The comparison is between neuron selectors only.
Canonical polysemantic neurons are not revisited.
Selector dependence (LAP/LAPE vs MAD/ConAct) concerns finding emotion-causal units, not whether a neuron counts as polysemantic.

record.verdict_notes: All rows are correctly linked to 'none'. The per-dataset tables (Appendix C) and Table 2 bear on no version either. Most models are 7B, though Audio Flamingo 3's size is not stated in the text. Kimi-Audio is the 7B Instruct version per Table 3, so r5–r8 and r17–r20 could record size 7B.

versions.untested_parts: No image-classifier neurons or mixed image inputs are studied.
No transformer language-model MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts are measured.
The study does not test superposition or capacity pressure as a cause of polysemanticity.
The study does not test initialization, regularization, training noise, or neuron capacity as causes of polysemanticity.
The study compares neuron-selection methods, not activation functions, architectures, or regularization effects on polysemantic-neuron share or performance costs.
The study does not revisit canonical polysemantic neurons or test whether their mixed inputs share a feature.
The study compares selectors for causal emotion effects, but does not measure how polysemanticity judgments change with activation range or explanation scoring.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

rows.locator_found: Table 1, Qwen2.5-Omni-7B self-effect, MAD -13.09 (= mean of Tables 5-7: -12.90, -16.90, -9.48)

relation.reason: The text never mentions polysemanticity or superposition, so 'discusses' would overstate it. It cites neuron-interpretability work only in passing, as related work or selector sources (Huben et al. 2024 SAE paper, Gurnee et al. 2024, Antverg & Belinkov 2022). Of the available categories, cites_only fits best.

tranche.reason: The study identifies emotion neurons and ablates or steers them. It never measures polysemanticity, does not use it as a tool, and tests no version.

source_check.notes: All six rows match Table 1 (r=0.5%), and the macro-averages check out against per-dataset Tables 5-7. The study never addresses polysemanticity, so rows linking to no version is correct. Audio Flamingo 3 is in Table 1 but has no rows in this pack. Kimi-Audio checkpoint is Kimi-Audio-7B-Instruct (Table 3).

statements.correction: Table 1 (r=0.5%, macro-avg over IEMOCAP/MELD/MSP-Podcast): self deactivation MAD/ConAct Qwen -13.09/-13.50, Kimi -13.63/-11.65, AF3 -15.17/-14.63; cross avg within |1.96|; steering self gain 1.94 to 3.35. Per-dataset (Tables 5-7): self -7.40 to -19.60, cross avg up to 3.40 / -3.85.
statements.problem: Minor: all figures are Table 1 macro-averages (over three datasets, and over other emotions for cross effects). Per-dataset values spread wider. The ranges are slightly wider than stated (self -11.65 to -15.17; steering +1.94 to +3.35), but the paper itself says 11-15 and +2 to +3.
